validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of 46,974 men examining supplemental zinc intake and incident prostate cancer with reported relative risks.

extraction.comparison_type: >100 mg/day supplemental zinc versus nonusers (advanced prostate cancer)
extraction.population: U.S. male health professionals in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study

sample_size.excerpt: We examined the association between supplemental zinc intake and prostate cancer risk among 46 974 U.S. men participating in the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study.

cases.excerpt: During 14 years of follow-up from 1986 through 2000, 2901 new cases of prostate cancer were ascertained, of which 434 cases were diagnosed as advanced cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: However, compared with nonusers, men who consumed more than 100 mg/day of supplemental zinc had a relative risk of advanced prostate cancer of 2.29 (95% confidence interval = 1.06 to 4.95; P(trend) =.003), and men who took supplemental zinc for 10 or more years had a relative risk of 2.37 (95% confidence interval = 1.42 to 3.95; P(trend)<.001).
